When that information is unavailable, Ingest uses a conservative maximum gap between consecutive frames from an identifiable camera, including its serial number. title: Send to Decks
keywords:
Select still photos in Browse or Apple Photos and choose  File → Send to Decks… , search for it in  ⌘K , use the photo or group context menu, or press  ⇧⌘E . Photos are sent in visible order. Video selections are not supported. 
 Choose  Original files  or  JPEG copies . JPEG copies offer dimensions, quality, file-size, sharpening, and metadata choices, with a prepared count and size before sending. Some RAW conversions use an embedded preview or companion JPEG and may contain less detail; the sheet explains this before sending. 
  Open in Decks for Mac  uses an installed compatible Mac app.

title: What you need
keywords: Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later and a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer). Intel Macs are not supported.    Apple Intelligence is optional.  Text-based metadata assistance requires macOS 26 or later; suggestions generated from photographs require macOS 27.   Apple Photos:  Editing captions, keywords, and native star ratings requires macOS 27. Other browsing and review features work on earlier supported versions.   To check your Mac, choose Apple menu → About This Mac. To install, open the disk image and drag Ingest to Applications.

title: Cameras and files it reads
keywords:
Ingest prefers an embedded camera preview or a paired JPEG / HEIF image. When a file needs RAW rendering, that slower first preview is handled separately and cached. Camera model and recording mode affect preview availability. 
 
 
   File  What happens   
 
  Sony  .ARW   Uses available embedded previews, choosing the size needed for the current view.  
  Fujifilm  .RAF   Reads the embedded JPEG where available.  
   .JPG  and  .JPEG   Reads the image and available embedded previews.  
   .HEIC ,  .HEIF , and  .HIF   Opens and browses.  
   .MP4  and  .MOV   Browses and plays, with a poster

title: The first hour
keywords:
The keys are the part worth learning, and there is a way to practice them that cannot hurt anything. Choose Help, then Open Practice Folder. Ingest builds about thirty throwaway images and opens them, and the status bar tells you which keys to try. Nothing in that folder matters, so tag, rate, label, and undo as roughly as you like. 
 Press  ?  at any time for the shortcut sheet, or  ⌘K  to search every command by name. Tap and release  ⌘ , then press and hold it again to see contextual shortcuts. The complete list lives on the  shortcuts page , and the  Getting started  guide walks one card

title: Updates
keywords:
Choose Ingest, then Check for Updates. Automatic checking is off until you turn it on in Settings, General. An update is only installed if it carries a signature made with my key. 
 What each version changed is in the  release notes . Update checks omit hardware profiling; the host receives normal connection information. The  privacy page  says exactly what does and does not leave the machine.

title: Coming from Photo Mechanic
keywords:
The habits carry over.  T  tags, the arrow keys move,  ⌘G  is ingest, and  {seqn}  is the saved sequence counter. The  naming reference  lists supported brace tokens; check your existing patterns against it. 
 Three differences worth knowing. Marking keys do not advance by default, and you can turn advancing on in Settings → Browsing. Tags are a simple on/off flag, independent of ratings and colors. The Filter panel offers All, Tagged, and Untagged, and the active filter can be cleared from the folder header. And stars and color labels use the Lightroom keys,  1  to  5  and  6  to  9 , saved

title: Memory cards
keywords:
Insert a card and it appears in the sources list with its name and free space. By default Ingest opens it for you. That is a setting in Settings → Transfers, if you would rather it just sat in the list. 
  Reviewing does not change your card originals.  Ratings, keywords, renaming, and Finder tags are applied to copies, not to files on the card. Source files are deleted only when you explicitly request it after copies have been verified at every destination. title: Thumbnails are slow or missing
keywords:
Preview speed depends on the camera format, available embedded image, storage, and connection. If browsing is slow, try a local copy to distinguish file-rendering work from a slow card reader, network volume, or file provider. 
 Thumbnails that are expensive to build are cached on disk, under 2 GB, and cleared from Settings, Advanced. Clearing the cache is safe and never touches a photograph. 
 A photograph with no thumbnail at all is usually a raw format Ingest cannot read yet. See  cameras and files it reads .

title: Review, focus peaking, or eye results look wrong
keywords: Eye and sharpness assessments are assistance, not final decisions. Inspect the face or detail at a useful zoom and check the original photo. Low-contrast detail can be sharp without a focus-peaking highlight. Uncertain face results need your judgment.  Review uses a fixed queue: marking a photograph does not remove it from that queue. Browse filters are separate. If expected photos are missing, check the active filter, collapsed stacks, and Subfolders.  Keys depend on context. title: A client pick list has missing or ambiguous matches
keywords: Open the intended folder or Photos collection first. Choose the correct match mode: Filenames / relative paths or Displayed image numbers. Numbers refer to the current displayed review order; they are not automatically camera filename suffixes.  Use a relative path to distinguish repeated filenames in different folders, or narrow the collection. Review the missing and ambiguous counts before Select Matches. Selecting matches does not apply ratings or tags.  Pick-list instructions →

title: Lightroom or Photos does not show my keywords
keywords:
Ingest writes metadata directly into supported rendered files and uses XMP sidecars for proprietary RAW files. Apple Photos may not read RAW sidecars. Export a JPEG with metadata and GPS included, then send that JPEG to Photos when those fields need to travel with the image. Native Photos edits are available separately in the Photos workspace, with caption, keyword, and rating writes requiring macOS 27.

title: I entered a location, but there is no map pin
keywords: Descriptive city, state, country, and place names are different from GPS coordinates. In Metadata Assist, type  ;loc , choose Map Location, and press Return. Search Apple Maps, select a result, review its pin, and apply it to the intended photos.  When checking another app, open the edited copies, not card originals. Apple Photos may not read a RAW XMP sidecar; export a JPEG with metadata and GPS included if those fields must travel.  GPS and descriptive locations →

title: Fujifilm Recipe is missing or incomplete
keywords: Select one supported Fujifilm JPEG, or a RAW + JPEG pair with a qualifying JPEG companion. The recipe section uses recorded JPEG camera settings; a RAW file alone does not qualify for this tool. Check Settings → Sidebar Information if the section is hidden.  Missing settings are omitted. Ingest does not guess a custom recipe name. Previously saved notes can differ from the detected settings; Use Camera Settings restores the detected draft while editing. Copy and Export produce reference text, not a camera-installable profile.  Fujifilm recipe guide →

title: My workspace or filenames are not right
keywords: Confirm the active workspace in the window toolbar. Open at Launch is a separate choice.  Open its setup and check required questions, the receiving folder, and Import File Names. New workspaces keep original filenames until you change that choice.  Connect an external destination. If its drive was renamed, reselect the folder.  Use Review & Save to inspect the examples, save the workspace, then check the actual output paths in Import Settings.   For continuing group numbers, choose the same shoot across cards. title: A copy did not finish
keywords:
Ingest copies to a temporary name, flushes it to disk, reads the copy back, compares it to the source, and only then gives it its real name. Nothing is ever overwritten. If something goes wrong part way, the files that were already copied and verified are kept and the rest are not, and the receipt records what happened. 
 
 The Import button is dim 
 The reason is printed beside it. The usual ones are no destination chosen, an empty All, Tagged, or Selected scope, a template that will not parse, or two photographs that would end up with the same name.

title: Backup strategy
keywords:
Use a separate physical drive for Photo Backup. Ingest’s second verified copy is one part of a backup workflow: arrange off-site protection and editor/catalog backups separately. 
 A  Lightroom catalog backup does not back up your original photographs . See  3-2-1 backup guidance  for keeping originals safe across media and locations. 
 Project folders that separate source photographs from outputs are an approach also used by  Capture One Sessions . They are not mandatory standards.

title: Lightroom, a Shortcut, or an after-import action did not run
keywords: Check the completion details for skipped or failed actions.  Check each action’s Photos for this action scope. Importing All does not mean an action set to Tagged receives every file.  Confirm the chosen app, Shortcut, or script is available on this Mac, and review any permission prompt.  Retry unfinished actions from the result when offered. Successful actions are left alone.   Open an action in Settings → Automation and test it on a small disposable selection when appropriate. Opening files in an editor and importing them into that editor’s catalog are separate steps. title: Permission prompts
keywords:
macOS asks before an app reads a removable volume. Allow it, or Ingest cannot see your cards. If you dismissed it, the switch is in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Files and Folders. 
 Connecting to Apple Photos or sending files to it requests Photos read/write permission. Ingest uses your System Photo Library, not an arbitrary library file. If Connect did nothing in an older beta, update to the current release and try again. If access was denied, choose Open Photos Privacy Settings, enable Ingest, and return to the app. Settings → General controls Apple Photos integration for the ap

title: Apple Photos availability
keywords: Native caption, keyword, and rating edits require macOS 27. Earlier supported versions keep Photos ratings local and provide native favorites, dates, and locations. Cloud-only media needs a working connection to Apple Photos. Offline iCloud transfers, switching System Photo Libraries, and playback across all Live Photo and video formats remain beta validation areas. Use  Import History  to review interrupted or uncertain imports before retrying.

title: Photos have not appeared in Decks
keywords: Send to Decks works with selected still photos and requires a compatible Decks receiver. For Open in Decks for Mac, check that the Mac app is installed. For iCloud, check Apple sign-in and connectivity, then review the transfer status in Ingest and Incoming Photos in Decks.  Decks waits for you to choose a new or existing project. Later leaves the transfer in Incoming Photos. Cloud-only Apple Photos images may first need to download. Review the saved transfer’s status before retrying. title: Claude Second Opinion
keywords: This optional feature needs Claude Code installed and signed in to your Claude subscription. It uses your account’s connection and usage limits. It is separate from the built-in on-device checks, which do not require Claude.  Review what Ask sends to Anthropic  before using it.

title: Get in touch
keywords: Email  contact@brianrenshaw.app  with your macOS version, the Ingest version from Settings, General, and your camera model. Tell me what you pressed and what happened. You never need to send me a photograph to report a problem.
